title: The SSF conformance PR added GET/PATCH/PUT stream handlers plus stream verify and status views without the add_stream provider permission check that the existing POST handler enforces, so any token holder for the app can read, modify, verify and disable its event streams.

findings.explanation: The diff does not introduce any SQL queries or raw SQL string concatenation. All changes are authorization checks using Django's permission framework (has_perm) and HTTP response generation. No user-controlled input is directly used in SQL construction.

The PR adds authorization checks to multiple stream endpoints (GET, PATCH, PUT, DELETE, POST verify, GET/POST status) by verifying that the user has the 'authentik_providers_ssf.add_stream' permission on the provider object before allowing access. Each method properly checks permissions and raises PermissionDenied if the user lacks the required permission. The test suite confirms these checks are enforced and correctly reject unauthorized users. The permission is checked against self.provider which is obtained from the request context in the parent SSFStreamView class.

evidence.content:
self.assertFalse(self.user.has_perm("authentik_providers_ssf.add_stream", self.provider))
        stream = Stream.objects.create(provider=self.provider)
        res = self.client.get(
            reverse(
                "authentik_providers_ssf:stream",
                kwargs={"application_slug": self.application.slug},
            ),
            HTTP_AUTHORIZATION=f"Bearer {self.token.token}",
        )
        self.assertEqual(res.status_code, 403)
